notes: A 2023 survey of 48 city blocks recorded an average summer afternoon temperature of 31.2 C where tree canopy covered less than 10 percent of the block.
Blocks with more than 40 percent canopy averaged 28.6 C on the same afternoons.
The survey covered only summer afternoons and did not record winter temperatures.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize the size of the temperature difference between the two kinds of blocks. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: Blocks with more than 40 percent canopy were 2.6 C cooler than the least-shaded blocks, at 28.6 C versus 31.2 C.
wrongs: Blocks with less than 10 percent canopy averaged 31.2 C on summer afternoons in the 2023 survey.
The 2023 survey measured 48 city blocks and recorded only summer afternoon temperatures.
Tree canopy covered more than 40 percent of some surveyed blocks and less than 10 percent of others.
why: This choice reports only the hottest group, so it does not compare the two groups.
This choice describes the method and its limits rather than the size of the difference.
This choice describes canopy coverage without mentioning any temperature.

notes: Bristlecone pines in the White Mountains of California are among the oldest living trees; one named Methuselah is estimated at 4,855 years old.
A study sampled 22 bristlecone pines and found that the oldest trees grow on dolomite, a dry and nutrient-poor rock.
Pines on adjacent moist granite sites were on average 1,200 years younger.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize the advantage of the harsh dolomite site. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: The pines sampled on dry dolomite averaged 1,200 years older than pines on nearby moist granite.
wrongs: Methuselah, a bristlecone pine in the White Mountains, has been estimated at 4,855 years old.
The study sampled 22 bristlecone pines growing in the White Mountains of California.
Bristlecone pines are among the oldest living trees, and some of them grow on dolomite.
why: This choice gives a single age but does not compare the two kinds of site.
This choice reports only the sample size and location, not any advantage.
This choice states a general fact without using the age comparison from the notes.

notes: Many noctuid moths have ears on their thorax that detect bat echolocation calls above 20 kHz.
In a flight-tunnel test, 87 percent of moths with intact ears turned away when a simulated bat call played.
Only 38 percent of moths whose ears had been sealed turned away.
The call was played at 70 decibels.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize how large the difference between the two groups was. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: Moths with working ears evaded the call 87 percent of the time, compared with only 38 percent when their ears were sealed.
wrongs: Noctuid moths have ears on their thorax that detect bat calls above 20 kHz.
The simulated bat call was played at 70 decibels inside a flight tunnel.
Researchers tested moths in a flight tunnel by playing a simulated bat call.
why: This choice explains the anatomy but gives no result from the test.
This choice reports a detail of the setup rather than any difference between groups.
This choice describes the procedure without reporting the outcome.

notes: A kestrel hovers by flapping into a headwind while holding its head still.
Researchers filmed 120 hovering bouts and found that birds used more wingbeats as wind speed rose from 2 to 6 m/s.
The birds also drifted more during gusts.
Hovering costs roughly 30 percent more energy than gliding.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize how stronger wind changes a kestrel's hovering. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: As wind rose from 2 to 6 m/s, kestrels flapped more often and drifted more during gusts.
wrongs: A kestrel hovers by flapping into a headwind while holding its head still.
Researchers filmed 120 hovering bouts in order to study kestrel flight.
Hovering costs a kestrel roughly 30 percent more energy than gliding does.
why: This choice describes hovering in general but not the effect of stronger wind.
This choice reports the size of the study rather than what the study found.
This choice compares hovering with gliding but says nothing about wind speed.

notes: Roman sea walls built with volcanic ash have survived about 2,000 years of wave action.
In those walls, seawater reacting with the ash formed a mineral called aluminous tobermorite.
That mineral strengthened the concrete over time.
Ordinary portland concrete weakens when exposed to seawater.
items.goal: The student wants to explain why the Roman sea walls lasted so long. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: Seawater reacting with volcanic ash formed aluminous tobermorite, a mineral that made the concrete stronger over time.
wrongs: Some Roman sea walls have survived about 2,000 years of wave action.
Concrete made with volcanic ash forms the same mineral that Roman concrete contained.
Ordinary portland concrete weakens when it is exposed to seawater.
why: This choice states how long the walls lasted but not why they lasted.
This choice identifies the mineral without explaining its strengthening effect.
This choice describes modern concrete rather than the Roman material.

notes: Seagrass meadows in Elkhorn Slough lost about 90 percent of their area between 1870 and 1980.
Sea otters returned to the slough in the 1980s.
By 2013 seagrass covered about 4,000 hectares, close to its historical extent.
Otters eat crabs that dig up seagrass roots.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize how complete the seagrass recovery was. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: After otters returned, seagrass in Elkhorn Slough recovered from a 90 percent loss to about 4,000 hectares by 2013.
wrongs: Sea otters returned to Elkhorn Slough in the 1980s and eat crabs that dig up seagrass roots.
Between 1870 and 1980, seagrass meadows in Elkhorn Slough lost about 90 percent of their area.
By 2013 seagrass covered about 4,000 hectares in Elkhorn Slough.
why: This choice explains the mechanism but does not describe the recovery.
This choice reports only the loss, not what happened afterward.
This choice gives the final area without the loss it recovered from, so the completeness is unclear.

notes: Lettuce grown under red-blue LED light reached harvest weight 20 percent faster than lettuce under white LED light.
Leaf length was nearly the same in both groups.
The trial used 300 plants per treatment.
Red-blue light used 12 percent less electricity.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize the energy advantage of red-blue lighting. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: Red-blue LED light used 12 percent less electricity while bringing lettuce to harvest weight 20 percent sooner than white LED.
wrongs: Lettuce under red-blue LED light reached harvest weight 20 percent faster than lettuce under white LED light.
The trial compared 300 plants per treatment and found leaf length was nearly the same in both groups.
Red-blue LED light and white LED light produced lettuce with nearly the same leaf length.
why: This choice emphasizes speed rather than the electricity saving.
This choice focuses on the design and leaf length, not on energy use.
This choice reports a similarity between the treatments, not an advantage.

notes: Periodical cicadas in Brood X emerge every 17 years.
Their prime-numbered cycles coincide with few predator population peaks.
A model found that a 17-year cycle overlaps with fewer predator peaks than a 12-year or 15-year cycle would.
Cicadas live underground for nearly the entire cycle.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize why a prime-numbered cycle may be advantageous. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: A 17-year cycle overlaps with fewer predator population peaks than a 12-year or 15-year cycle would, the model found.
wrongs: Periodical cicadas in Brood X emerge every 17 years.
Cicadas spend nearly their entire lives underground before emerging to breed.
A model compared 17-year cycles with 12-year and 15-year cycles.
why: This choice states the cycle length without explaining any advantage.
This choice describes the life history but not the effect on predators.
This choice describes the model without reporting its result.

notes: Honeybees signal the direction of food by waggling at an angle to vertical.
Researchers recorded 260 dances from four colonies.
Colonies in open farmland danced more often and for longer than colonies in dense forest.
Longer dances recruit more foragers.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize the link between habitat and recruitment. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: Farmland colonies danced more often and longer than forest colonies, and longer dances recruit more foragers.
wrongs: Honeybees signal the direction of food by waggling at an angle to vertical.
Researchers recorded 260 dances from four honeybee colonies.
Colonies in dense forest danced less often than colonies in open farmland.
why: This choice explains the dance but says nothing about habitat or recruitment.
This choice reports only the sample size.
This choice notes the habitat difference but omits its link to recruiting foragers.

notes: A Kansas prairie remnant was burned every one, two, or four years over 20 years.
Milkweed stems peaked at 412 per hectare under two-year burns.
Annual burns produced 96 stems per hectare.
Four-year burns produced 203 stems per hectare.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize which burn interval was best for milkweed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: Two-year burns produced 412 milkweed stems per hectare, more than annual burns or four-year burns did.
wrongs: The Kansas prairie remnant was burned every one, two, or four years over a 20-year period.
Annual burns produced 96 milkweed stems per hectare, the fewest of the three intervals.
Four-year burns produced 203 milkweed stems per hectare.
why: This choice describes the experiment but gives no result.
This choice reports the weakest treatment without comparing it with the best.
This choice reports one middle result without identifying the best interval.

notes: Court records from Istanbul list 643 coffeehouses operating in 1680.
Many were shut after a 1683 decree.
Records show that 120 had reopened within two years.
The records name neighborhoods but not owners.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize how quickly the coffeehouses returned. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: After a 1683 decree closed many Istanbul coffeehouses, 120 of them reopened within two years.
wrongs: Court records from Istanbul list 643 coffeehouses operating in 1680.
Many Istanbul coffeehouses were shut after a decree in 1683.
The court records name neighborhoods but do not name the owners of the coffeehouses.
why: This choice gives the number before the closures, not the speed of return.
This choice mentions the closure without any reopening.
This choice describes what the records omit rather than what they show.

notes: Shipworms bore into wood using tiny shells.

Industrial breakdown of cellulose usually requires high heat.
items.goal: The student wants to emphasize the industrial promise of the shipworm enzyme. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: A shipworm gut enzyme broke down cellulose at room temperature, a step industry usually needs high heat for.
wrongs: Shipworms bore into wood using tiny shells on their bodies.
Bacteria in the shipworm gut produce enzymes that break down cellulose.
Industrial breakdown of cellulose usually requires high heat.
why: This choice describes how shipworms bore, not the enzyme's promise.
This choice identifies the source of the enzymes without saying why that matters.
This choice describes the industrial problem but not the shipworm solution.

notes: Alpine marmots whistle when predators approach.
Recordings of 88 alarm calls showed that whistles differ by predator type.
Calls for aerial predators had more high-frequency notes.
Marmots responded faster to calls for aerial predators.

items.correct: Whistles for aerial predators have more high-frequency notes, and marmots responded faster to those calls.
wrongs: Alpine marmots whistle when a predator approaches.
Researchers recorded 88 alarm calls from Alpine marmots.
Calls for aerial predators had more high-frequency notes than other calls.
why: This choice states only that marmots whistle, not that the calls differ.
This choice reports the sample size without any finding.
This choice describes the acoustic difference but not the response it produced.

notes: A bamboo bicycle frame weighed 2.9 kg, about the same as an aluminum frame.
Bamboo frames absorbed 40 percent more road vibration in laboratory tests.
The bamboo frame cost 60 percent less to build locally.

items.goal: The student wants to emphasize the cost advantage of the bamboo frame. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
items.correct: The bamboo frame cost 60 percent less to build locally than an aluminum frame while weighing about the same.
wrongs: Bamboo frames absorbed 40 percent more road vibration than aluminum frames in laboratory tests.

Bamboo bicycle frames have not been tested for durability beyond 8,000 km.

notes: Researchers tagged 32 whale sharks off Ningaloo Reef.

wrongs: Researchers tagged 32 whale sharks off Ningaloo Reef.

Whale sharks were previously thought to feed mainly near the surface.

items.correct: Beans fermented in wooden boxes had more yeast diversity, which correlated with stronger fruity notes in blind tastings.

Fermenting cacao beans develops flavor through the action of yeast and bacteria.

items.correct: Serrated trailing edges cut noise by 3 decibels without changing power output, though manufacturing cost rose about 2 percent.
wrongs: Researchers recorded blade-tip noise at 40 wind turbines.
Blades with serrated trailing edges were 3 decibels quieter than standard blades.
Power output was unchanged when blades had serrated trailing edges.

Mugs labeled lead-free were not exempt.

notes: Seedlings planted with native fungi survived 32 percent better.
